output.summary:
I ran one engine mutation per test with `srdloop mutate` (a no-op control mutation passed, as it should). 53 of the 57 tests failed when the rule they cover was broken, so I keep them. I refute 3 and send 1 to a person.

**Refuted:**
- `test_a_wizard_cant_cast_bless` (0.65): the engine refuses because the wizard hasn't prepared Bless, not because Bless is off the wizard's spell list. `castable()` never checks class lists, and making `_way` accept the cast changed nothing.
- `test_a_creature_60_feet_away_cant_be_blessed` (0.6): anything that refuses a target at 35 ft also refuses one at 60 ft, and the clean-refusal helper already checks that no slot was spent. The 35 ft test covers it.
- `test_four_targets_with_a_level_1_slot_blesses_nobody` (0.6): this repeats `..._is_refused_cleanly` with the same setup, whose refusal helper already compares the whole game snapshot.

**Sent to a person:**
- `test_a_holy_symbol_worth_exactly_5_gp_is_enough` (0.45): it almost duplicates `test_bless_with_a_holy_symbol_works`, because the default Holy Symbol already costs 5 GP. Its explicit price may still be worth keeping.

**Weaker cases among the keeps:**
- `test_bless_without_a_holy_symbol_is_refused` still passes when the costed-component check is turned off, because the general material check refuses it with the same message. It does fail when the material check is removed, so it stays.
- `test_a_level_2_slot_doesnt_raise_the_d4` catches a wrong die size, but nothing ties the die size to the slot level, so it can't catch the specific bug its name describes.

**SRD wording:** none of the tests contradicts the text. Range, the costed Holy Symbol component, Concentration up to 1 minute, up to three creatures and attack rolls and saves only all follow from the unit. The 2014 holy water component is only used as a negative case. The readings the text doesn't settle (the caster blessing themself, death saves, a target that moves out of range) cite register rulings R-12, R-13 and R-14.
